turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good afternoon, Mrs.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ousu.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Nice to see you again. Just so we have the right chart, can you give me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Abina Ousu. November 19th,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Perfect.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Did your daughter bring you today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes. FU had dropped me at the door. She's parking the car. You can call her if you need anything. Her number is 555 -0148.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good, I'll keep that on file. So this is your six -month check on the atrial fibrillation. How have you been feeling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Mostly fine. I don't feel the heart racing like before. Sometimes, I'm a little tired in the afternoon, but I'm 74, you know.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Fair enough any shortness of breath, dizziness, or chest pain.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, none of that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's go over your medicines. You're on epixabin, five milligrams twice a day, and metaprolol six and eight, 25 milligrams.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The epixabin, yes. Morning and night, but the metaprolol is 50 now. You went up to 50 in April, remember?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're right, I see it here, 50 milligrams once a day, and the lisinopril, 10 milligrams in the morning for the blood pressure. Yes,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and I also take a baby aspirin every day now. My friend Ruth said it's good for the heart, so I started it in the summer. And my fish oil, one thousand milligrams.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, I'm glad you told me. That's actually something I want to talk about. Have you noticed any bleeding?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My gums bleed a little when I brush. And I had one nosebleed in August, but it stopped on its own, after about 10 minutes. And it hasn't happened again.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any black or tarry stools or blood in your urine?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any falls since I last saw you?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No falls, thank God. I walk with my church group twice a week.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: That's great, okay, your blood pressure is 132 over 78 and your pulse is 72 and irregular, which is expected with the atrial fibrillation. Weight is 148 pounds, same as last time. Heart is irregularly irregular,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: no murmur.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Lungs are clear and no swelling in your ankles.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. We did an ECG today.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: It shows atrial fibrillation with a rate of 74, so your rate is well controlled on the metaprolol. Your labs from last month look good too. Hemoglobin was 12 .9 and kidney function was normal created 9 -0.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 9. So the blood is okay?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Yes, no sign that you're losing blood. Now let me explain the balance. Your stroke risk score is three, because of your age being a woman and the high blood pressure. That's high enough that the epixabon really protects you from a stroke, and your dose of five milligrams twice a day is the right one for your age, weight, and kidneys.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The flip side is bleeding. Your bleeding risk score is two right now, and one of those points is the aspirin. Aspirin. Taking aspirin on top of epixabon raises the bleeding risk quite a bit and for your heart it doesn't add protection. So I'd like you to stop the aspirin.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oh, Ruth will be surprised. Okay, I'll stop it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ruth's situation may be different. For you, the epixabon is doing the job. The fish oil at that dose is fine to keep. Use a soft toothbrush and mention the gums to your dentist at your next cleaning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I can do that.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: So, to sum up, this is permanent atrial fibrillation, rate controlled on long -term anticoagulation, and your blood pressure is at goal. Keep the epixubin 5 milligrams twice a day, metaprolol 6 and 8 50 milligrams once a day, and lisinopril 10 milligrams. Stop the aspirin. We'll check a blood count again in three months. You can do that at the lab on 2210 Wexford Avenue.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yes, that's close to my house.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Call us if you see black stools, blood in the urine, or a nosebleed that won't stop after 20 minutes, and if you ever fall and hit your head, go to the emergency room, even if you feel fine because of the blood thinner.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, I'll remember.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'll see you back in six months. Say hi to Effuel for me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I will. Thank you, Doctor.
